2027-05-01.title: Saturday of the Fifth Week of Easter
readings: Come over to Macedonia and help us
Make a joyful noise to the Lord, all the earth (or: Alleluia)
If the world hates you, be aware that it hated me before it hated you
2027-05-01.alt: Saturday of the Fifth Week of Easter (Year I). Optional memorial of St Joseph the Worker: the weekday readings are given here; the proper readings of the memorial, Genesis 1:26–2:3 or Colossians 3:14–15, 17, 23–24, with Psalm 90 and Matthew 13:54–58, may be used instead. In India 1 May is also May Day, Labour Day. Today the month of May, dedicated to the Blessed Virgin Mary, begins. Liturgical colour: white.
2027-05-01.verse: If the world hates you, be aware that it hated me before it hated you.
theo: Paul sets out on his second missionary journey, and the first thing Luke tells us is about a young man. In Lystra, the town where Paul had once been stoned and left for dead, there is a disciple named Timothy, “the son of a Jewish woman who was a believer; but his father was a Greek.” The believers speak well of him, and Paul wants him as a companion. Then the little band travels from town to town, handing on the decisions of the apostles and elders in Jerusalem, “so the churches were strengthened in the faith and increased in numbers daily.” What follows is strange. The missionaries try to preach in the province of Asia, and the Holy Spirit forbids them. They try to go north into Bithynia, and “the Spirit of Jesus did not allow them.” Two doors close, one after the other. They end up at Troas, on the coast, with nowhere obvious to go. And there, in the night, Paul sees a man of Macedonia standing and pleading: “Come over to Macedonia and help us.” At once they cross the sea. Notice the small change in the text: from this verse Luke begins to write “we.” The writer has joined the journey. The Gospel is about to enter Europe, and it enters through closed doors, a dream in the night, and a plea for help.

The Gospel moves from the joy of the mission to its cost. At the Last Supper Jesus warns his friends: “If the world hates you, be aware that it hated me before it hated you.” In John's Gospel “the world” here does not mean the earth God made and loves (John 3:16), but human life organised without God and against him. The disciple who belongs to Christ will not always be welcome in it. “Remember the word that I said to you, ‘Servants are not greater than their master.’ If they persecuted me, they will persecute you; if they kept my word, they will keep yours also.” Paul would learn this soon enough in Macedonia: beatings in Philippi, riots in Thessalonica. And yet the plea “help us” was real. The same world that resists the Gospel is crying out for it. Today, on the first of May, the Church also honours St Joseph the Worker. Pope Pius XII gave this memorial to the Church in 1955, so that the workers' day would also be a day of the carpenter of Nazareth. The people of Nazareth once asked of Jesus, “Is not this the carpenter's son?” Joseph's hidden work, with the Blessed Virgin Mary beside him, made a home where the Son of God grew up. On this day we pray for all who work, for all who cannot find work, and for all whose work is unjust or unsafe; and we begin the month of May with the Mother of Jesus.
outline: Ask: when a door closes in your life, do you see a wall or a signpost?
Point 1 · The Spirit closes two doors
Asia and Bithynia forbidden; the way to Macedonia opened.
Point 2 · Come over and help us
The cry of a world that needs the Gospel.
Disciples share the lot of their Master.
St Joseph the Worker and the dignity of work.
“Come over to Macedonia and help us.”
live: Think of one plan of yours that failed recently. Ask the Holy Spirit in prayer: Lord, where are you leading me instead?
Do your work today, at home or outside, as done for the Lord, and thank one worker whom people usually ignore: a cleaner, a driver, a cook, a watchman.
2027-05-01.prayer: Lord Jesus, risen from the dead, you sent your apostles across the sea in answer to the cry “Come over and help us.” When our plans fail and doors close, give us the humility to follow your Spirit. When the world resists your word, keep us faithful, for you were hated before us. Through the prayers of St Joseph, the carpenter of Nazareth, bless all who work and all who look for work, and give us a share in the Easter joy of your Mother, whose month begins today. Amen.
altar: At the offertory the priest calls the bread “fruit of the earth and work of human hands” and the wine “fruit of the vine and work of human hands.” On this day of St Joseph the Worker, our work is carried to the altar with them, and the Lord changes that bread and wine into his own Body and Blood. Nothing we do in honest labour is lost if it is offered with him.

quick: Paul took the young Timothy as companion; the Holy Spirit closed the way to Asia and Bithynia.
In a night vision a Macedonian pleaded, “Come over and help us,” and the Gospel crossed into Europe.
Jesus warned that the world which hated him would hate his disciples; today is also St Joseph the Worker and the first day of Mary's month.
2027-05-01.action: Thank one worker today by name, and offer your own work to God at the start of the day.
2027-05-01.question: When God closes a door for me, do I complain, or do I look for where the Spirit is leading?
kidsaint: Joseph was a carpenter in the village of Nazareth. Every day he worked with wood, making doors, tables and ploughs, and Jesus learned to work beside him. Joseph did not become famous, but he worked hard and honestly to look after Jesus and Mary. Lesson: when we do our work well, even homework and helping at home, we can offer it to God like St Joseph.

family.explain: Paul wanted to go to some places, but the Holy Spirit said no. Then one night Paul had a dream of a man saying, “Come and help us!” So Paul and his friends went across the sea to a new country and told people about Jesus. Today we also remember St Joseph, who worked as a carpenter, and we begin May, Mother Mary's month.
family.intention: We pray for fathers and mothers who work hard for the family, and for people who have no job.
family.ask: Ask: “What work can each of us offer to God this week, like St Joseph?” Begin a family Rosary or one decade every evening this May.

illus: A young engineer from Thrissur had everything arranged for a job abroad. Twice the visa was refused, and he was bitter. In the waiting months he began teaching mathematics in the evenings to children of daily-wage workers in his parish, just to fill the time. Twenty children came, then fifty. When at last the visa came through, he turned it down. He says now: I thought God had shut the door; he had only shown me the right one.

pm.open: Come, Holy Spirit, lead us as you led Paul. St Joseph, pray for us. Amen.
share: The Spirit of Jesus did not allow them (Acts 16:7). When has a closed door in my life turned out to be God's guidance?
Come over to Macedonia and help us (Acts 16:9). Whose cry for help am I being asked to hear?
If the world hates you, be aware that it hated me before it hated you (John 15:18). Have I ever been mocked or left out because of my faith? How did I respond?
pm.resp: Make a joyful noise to the Lord, all the earth.
interc: For missionaries who go where they are needed, that they may follow the Holy Spirit with courage.
For workers, especially daily-wage labourers, migrants and those in unsafe jobs, that they may receive a just wage and be treated with dignity.
For the unemployed and for young people looking for their first job.
For Christians who suffer hostility because of their faith.
For our families, that this month of May may be a month of prayer with the Blessed Virgin Mary.
pm.close: Father, you call us to share in your work of creation and to follow your Son, the carpenter's son. Through the prayers of St Joseph, make our work holy and our hearts open to your Spirit. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Paul and his companions had good plans. They wanted to preach in Asia; the Holy Spirit said no. They tried Bithynia; the Spirit of Jesus did not allow them (Acts 16:7). Two closed doors. And then, at Troas, by the sea, a dream: a man of Macedonia saying, come over to Macedonia and help us (Acts 16:9).

We do not like closed doors. An exam failed, a job refused, a marriage proposal that did not work out, a transfer we did not want. But sometimes God closes a door to keep us for another. Paul did not sit down and sulk at Troas. He prayed, he listened, and when the call came he crossed the sea at once. Because of that crossing, the Gospel came to Europe.

Jesus is honest with us in the Gospel. Not every door will be opened by the world. If the world hates you, be aware that it hated me before it hated you (John 15:18). The servant is not greater than the master. Paul would be beaten in Philippi only days after he landed. Following the Spirit is not always comfortable. But it is always fruitful.

Today is also the first of May, and the Church shows us St Joseph the Worker. People in Nazareth looked down a little on Jesus: is not this the carpenter's son? But Joseph's hidden, honest work kept the Holy Family alive. Let us offer our work to God today, pray for every worker and for those who have no work, and begin this month of May close to our Mother Mary. Amen.
kids: Children, Paul wanted to go somewhere, but God said no. Then God showed him in a dream a man saying: come and help us! So Paul went, and many people came to know Jesus. Sometimes when we do not get what we want, God has a better plan. And today we remember St Joseph, the carpenter who worked hard for Jesus and Mary. Let us help at home today, like Jesus helped Joseph!

intro: Theme: “Come over to Macedonia and help us.”
Doors closed by the Spirit, a cry for help, the cost of discipleship, and the carpenter of Nazareth.

q: The human mind plans the way, but the Lord directs the steps.
When they had come opposite Mysia, they attempted to go into Bithynia, but the Spirit of Jesus did not allow them;
points.apply: Bring one disappointment of this year to the Lord in prayer and ask, not why, but where: where are you leading me now?

q: Then I heard the voice of the Lord saying, “Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?” And I said, “Here am I; send me!”
During the night Paul had a vision: there stood a man of Macedonia pleading with him and saying, “Come over to Macedonia and help us.”
points.apply: Listen this week for one person's plea for help that you have been ignoring, and answer it.

q: More in number than the hairs of my head are those who hate me without cause
Remember the word that I said to you, ‘Servants are not greater than their master.’ If they persecuted me, they will persecute you; if they kept my word, they will keep yours also.
points.apply: Pray by name for one persecuted Christian community today, and do not be ashamed to make the sign of the cross in public.

sub: May Day and the month of Mary.
q: The Lord God took the man and put him in the garden of Eden to till it and keep it.
Whatever your task, put yourselves into it, as done for the Lord and not for your masters,
points.apply: Begin each working day this week with a short offering: Lord, I do this work for you; St Joseph, pray for me.

concl: The Spirit who closed two doors opened a third, and the Gospel crossed the sea in answer to a cry for help.
The disciple will share the Master's rejection, but also his fruitfulness; and with St Joseph and the Blessed Virgin Mary, our daily work becomes part of that mission.
2027-05-01.resolve: Offer your work to God each morning this May and pray one decade of the Rosary each evening.
